extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff, disciplinary counsel and courts
extracted.subtask_description: An Amended Final Order under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 imposing reciprocal discipline (suspension) on a registered patent practitioner and setting procedural and substantive conditions for suspension, reinstatement, publication, account restrictions, and future use of the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director may seek reciprocal discipline identical to that imposed by a state authority; respondent is provided an opportunity to oppose such reciprocal discipline based on the reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order requested that the Director impose reciprocal discipline identical to the Indiana Supreme Court's April 5, 2024 Order. If respondent fails to timely respond, the Office may determine there is no issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and impose reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and opportunity to respond (40 days)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must be given notice and an opportunity to file a response opposing reciprocal discipline within forty (40) days as provided in the Notice and Order and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order delivered on December 26, 2024 provided 40 days to file a response; Respondent's failure to file a response supported a determination of no material fact issue and imposition of discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imposition of suspension (not to exceed five years)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is suspended from the practice of patent, trademark, and other non-patent law before the USPTO for a period of time not to exceed five (5) years from the date of the final order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The suspension is based on violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h) and predicated upon an indefinite suspension by a state authority (Indiana Supreme Court).

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension continues until reinstatement under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall be suspended from practice before the USPTO until the OED Director grants a petition requesting reinstatement pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if a five-year cap is specified, reinstatement is controlled by the petition/review process in § 11.60 and the OED Director's grant of reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions permitting petition for reinstatement prior to five years
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent may file a petition requesting reinstatement prior to five years only if specific conditions (a–d) are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The four specified conditions are: (a) Indiana Supreme Court enters a final order converting the indefinite suspension to a definite suspension of less than five years; (b) Respondent provides a certified copy of that final order with any petition; (c) the petition is filed after Respondent successfully completes a suspension period equal to the definite period imposed by the Indiana Supreme Court; and (d) Respondent has fully complied with all provisions of 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 relating to a suspended or excluded practitioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with the obligations and requirements set forth in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 relating to suspended or excluded practitioners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance with § 11.58 is an express condition of any reinstatement petition and of the suspension order itself; failure to comply may affect reinstatement eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic publication of Final Order (FOIA Reading Room)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order at OED's electronic FOIA Reading Room (http://foiadocuments.uspto.gov).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary decisions are made available for public review at the OED FOIA Reading Room and the specific Final Order will be posted there.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication in the Official Gazette with specified notice content
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the provided notice describing the suspension, grounds (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)), and reinstatement conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Official Gazette notice should include respondent's name, registration number, nature of the reciprocal suspension, the predicate state action and rules, and the conditions under which a petition for reinstatement may be filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to state disciplinary agencies, courts, and the public (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall give notice of the public discipline and the reasons for it to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the states where respondent is admitted, to courts where respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public, pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order requires dissemination of the discipline information to relevant agencies and courts as part of public notice obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation from Customer Numbers and verified Electronic System accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent's name shall be dissociated from any Customer Number(s) and USPTO verified Electronic System account(s); respondent shall not apply for, obtain, nor have his/her name added to a USPTO Customer Number or a USPTO verified Electronic System account unless and until reinstated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prevents the suspended practitioner from using or being listed on any USPTO customer/account records until reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO authorization to disable or suspend USPTO.gov accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO is authorized to disable or suspend any USPTO.gov accounts registered to Respondent as of the date of the Final Order (including all accounts respondent has ever established, sponsored, or used in connection with any patent, trademark, or other matter before the USPTO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorization extends to accounts ever established, sponsored, or used by respondent; disabling/suspending is within USPTO discretion under the order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on applying for, obtaining, or using USPTO.gov verified Electronic System accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall not apply for or obtain a USPTO verified Electronic System account, nor have his/her name added to one, unless and until reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an express bar on obtaining or being added to verified accounts while suspended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on using, accessing, or assisting others to use USPTO.gov filing systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is prohibited from using, accessing, or assisting others in using or accessing any USPTO.gov account(s) or other USPTO filing systems for preparing or filing documents with the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prohibits circumvention of the suspension by having others file on respondent's behalf or by using any USPTO electronic filing resource.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific listed prohibitions until petition is granted
rubrics_metrics.description: Until a petition seeking reinstatement is granted pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60, respondent is prohibited (and the USPTO is authorized to disallow respondent) from: (1) opening/activating USPTO.gov account(s) for preparing or filing documents; (2) applying for or attempting to apply for such accounts; (3) verifying or attempting to verify any other person's credentials in connection with such accounts; and (4) sponsoring or attempting to sponsor USPTO.gov accounts for preparing or filing documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order explicitly enumerates these four prohibitions to prevent account creation, credential verification, and sponsorship activities while suspended.

rubrics_metrics.name: No obligation on USPTO to re-activate disabled/suspended accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order does not obligate the USPTO to take action, sua sponte, to re-activate any USPTO.gov account disabled or suspended pursuant to the order; it is respondent's sole responsibility to initiate any such re-activation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent must request/seek re-activation after reinstatement; the USPTO has no duty to automatically restore accounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of disciplinary record in future proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may consider the record of this disciplinary proceeding, including the Final Order, in future matters: (1) when addressing any further complaint or evidence of the same or similar misconduct; and/or (2) in any future disciplinary proceeding against respondent as an aggravating factor, to rebut any statement by respondent, and/or in connection with any request for reconsideration under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order makes the record available for use in aggravation, rebuttal, or reconsideration in subsequent disciplinary contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service by certified mail per 37 C.F.R. § 11.11(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order (Amended Final Order pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24) was mailed by first-class certified mail, return receipt requested, to respondent at the most recent address provided pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.11(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper service by mail to the address on file is required for the Notice and Order; certificate of service documents mailing and addresses used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for reciprocal discipline: violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)
rubrics_metrics.description: The discipline was imposed for violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h), predicated upon respondent being indefinitely suspended from practice by a state authority for failure to cooperate with a disciplinary investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Official Gazette notice explains the state-court predicate (Indiana suspension pursuant to Indiana Admission and Discipline Rule 23(10.1)(c)) and that the USPTO action is taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
